rationale:
The reviewed tests adequately cover `requirements.sdk.graph.agent-calls.agent_context`. I read only the supplied test sources and did not request any implementation source. Each obligation maps to a test and an assertion as follows.

- **`String` and `str` render their own text, and `&str` works through `&C`.** `fn[string_and_str_contexts_deliver_identical_prefixes_and_fingerprints]` sends both `text.to_owned()` and `&str` for `""` and `"héllo\0\n\npolicy"`. It asserts that the delivered prefix equals the text and that the fingerprint equals `context_fingerprint(text)`. The inputs include non-ASCII text and a NUL byte.
- **`&C` forwards to the referenced value.** `.context(&context)` with a custom type is exercised in `fn[contexts_render_once_allow_non_send_values_and_hash_exact_prefix_text]`. `&custom` as a tuple element is exercised in `fn[every_heterogeneous_tuple_arity_renders_elements_in_order]`.
- **`[C]` and `Vec<C>` render in order with a two-newline separator, and an empty collection renders `""`.**
  - The slice and `to_vec()` cases in the `string_and_str…` test both produce `"policy\n\nquestion"`.
  - `Vec::<String>::new()` is checked through the request. It delivers `""` with the empty-prefix fingerprint.
  - `let empty: &[String] = &[]` is checked directly in the tuple test and renders `""`.
- **Tuples of 2 through 12 render in order, separated by two newlines.** `fn[every_heterogeneous_tuple_arity_renders_elements_in_order]` asserts the exact string for every arity from 2 to 12. The tuples are heterogeneous, with a custom type followed by `String`s. The test also asserts `custom.renders.get() == 11`. The 12-`String` tuple appears in the first test.
- **Nesting and repeated elements are preserved.** The tuple `(vec!["a","a"], "b")` is asserted to render `"a\n\na\n\nb"`. A tuple of `(String, String)` is passed through `.context`.
- **`.context(value)` obtains the text once and keeps no borrow of `value`.**
  - The first test uses a `CountingContext` and asserts one render after two `.context` calls.
  - It mutates `context.text` after building the request and asserts that the delivered prefix is still `"héllo…"`. That mutation would not compile if the builder kept a borrow.
  - The `string_and_str…` test clears a `String` after `.context(temporary.as_str())` and still passes.
- **The value needs no `Hash`, `Serialize`, `Send` or `Sync`.** `CountingContext` holds an `Rc` and a `Cell`, so it is non-`Send`. It is used successfully, and the resulting future is asserted `Send`.
- **Repeated calls use the same separator.** `.context("policy").context("question")` yields `"policy\n\nquestion"`. That is the same as the tuple, slice and `Vec` forms.
- **No context calls give an empty prefix with the same fingerprint as an explicitly empty prefix.** `ctx.ask::<Answer>().await` is compared with `context_fingerprint("")`. The test also asserts that no node inputs were supplied for that request.
- **The fingerprint hashes the exact UTF-8 prefix with a versioned scheme.** `fn[prefix_hashes_match_known_utf8_sha256_without_normalization]` pins known SHA-256 values and the `context-prefix-sha256-v1` scheme tag. It also checks that NFC and NFD forms, and different amounts of whitespace, differ. Together with the exact-prefix assertions, this shows no normalization.
- **The fingerprint preserves order and repetition.** `"a\n\nb"` and `"b\n\na"` have different fingerprints. Repeated elements appear in the delivered, hashed text.
- **The fingerprint does not depend on type identity or object addresses.** `String`, `&str`, tuple, slice and `Vec` forms of the same text all hash to the same fingerprint.
- **Node inputs, the result schema and the rest of the request are outside the fingerprint.** In the `string_and_str…` test:
  - Requests with `contents_of_current_node` and `contents_of_successors` carry node inputs. They have the same text-derived fingerprint as the plain request.
  - A `Value` schema request and an `Answer` schema request have the same fingerprint.
  - A request from node 2 has the same fingerprint as the others.
  - A request with a different `requests[..].3` value still has the same fingerprint.

Two unexercised cases remain: nested tuples, and a one-element collection. The requirement names neither as a distinct boundary, and the same code paths are covered by the tests above, so I count neither as a gap. The `public_exports_match_the_appendix` test in `public_api.rs` only checks the export inventory. I treated it as supporting evidence and did not rely on it for behavior.

text: :::{req} agent_context
Supplies reusable prompt text for an agent request. `contents` may borrow or own the string.
The SDK implements this trait for the following combinations:
| Value | Rendering |
| `String` | Use its text directly. |
| `str` | Use its text directly; `&str` works through the reference implementation. |
| `&C`, where `C: Context + ?Sized` | Forward to the referenced value. |
| `[C]` and `Vec<C>`, where `C: Context` | Render elements in order, separated by two newlines. An empty collection renders an empty string. |
| Heterogeneous tuples of 2 through 12 `Context` values | Render elements in order, separated by two newlines. |
Combinations can nest and preserve repeated elements. Each `.context(value)`
call obtains the text once and retains it for both the prefix and its hash,
without retaining a borrow of `value`. The value needs no `Hash`, `Serialize`,
`Send`, or `Sync` implementation. Repeated calls use the same two-newline
separator as combinations. No context calls give the empty prefix and the
same fingerprint as an explicitly empty rendered prefix.
The cache fingerprint hashes the exact UTF-8 prefix delivered to the agent,
using a versioned scheme. It preserves order and repetition and uses neither
object addresses nor type identities. It identifies this prefix, including the
question; node inputs, the result schema, and the rest of the request are outside
that fingerprint.
